title: Evaluering av tilskuddsordninger for nasjonale minoriteters språk og kultur
description: Kulturdirektoratet forvalter fem tilskuddsordninger for å styrke nasjonale minoriteters språk, kultur, identitet og egenorganisering. De nasjonale minoritetene i Norge er kvener/norskfinner, skogfinner, romanifolk/tatere, romer og jøder. Ordningene er sentrale virkemidler for aktiv samfunnsdeltakelse og styrking av språk og kultur. På oppdrag fra Kommunal- og distriktsdepartementet lyser Kulturdirektoratet nå ut en ekstern evaluering av disse ordningene. Formålet med evalueringen er å få kunnskap om hvorvidt, i hvilken grad og på hvilken måte tilskuddsordningene bidrar til å oppfylle målene som er satt og hvordan de eventuelt kan videreutvikles for bedre å styrke nasjonale minoriteters språk og kultur. Oppdragstaker skal vurdere om ordningene er effektive med hensyn til ressursbruk, organisering og måloppnåelse.

title: J061--ELECTRICAL TESTING (SOLICITATION)
description: 3-Year Electrical Testing and Repair Contract Performance Work Statement (PWS) General Requirements: Contractor shall furnish all supplies, materials, equipment, personnel/labor and technical supervision required to perform inspections, repairs, testing, cleaning, calibrations and adjustments on the electrical power distribution system and associated equipment at the Hampton Veterans Affairs Medical Center within the allotted time frame of this contract. This is a 4160 volt primary system that includes various secondary voltages and both emergency and normal power sources. A comprehensive list of equipment is included in this contract as well as a dollar amount to be set aside for repairs. All inspections and testing procedures must meet the criteria of the original equipment manufacturer along with the latest editions of the following codes, standards and specifications listed: ANSI, IEEE, ICEA, NETA, NEMA, NFPA, JCAHO and VA regulations. The contractor shall be responsible for supplying all portable power required to power up any and all test equipment necessary throughout these tests. The use of normal or emergency building power will not be allowed. The contractor shall be responsible for securing all manufacturers information, curves, data, procedures and any other information necessary to conduct specific tests on equipment and systems. Prior to beginning field-testing, the testing organization shall submit test procedures and a detailed test schedule to the Electrical Supervisor for each item of equipment to be field-tested. No testing is to be performed until after the test procedures and schedules have been approved. The contractor shall be responsible for all coordination between Dominion Virginia Power (if applicable), station supervisory personnel and test personnel for scheduling shut-downs, system tests and tests on system components. The V.A Medical Center Electrical Staff will be responsible for conducting the actual scheduled outages and reenergizing of circuits and components on V.A. premises and V.A. owned equipment only. Lockout/Tagout of this equipment will be performed jointly between the V. A. Medical Center Electricians and the Contractor. The contractor will be responsible for removal and replacement of any and all breakers needing to be tested. All breakers being removed will be properly reinstalled. Any and all conductors removed from a breaker will be properly terminated back to that breaker and any and all lugs will be properly torqued to manufacturers specifications. Testing shall commence and be completed within nine (9) consecutive days, beginning on a Saturday and ending on the following Sunday. The specific dates shall be coordinated with the COTR. All outages shall be scheduled with the COTR two weeks in advance of testing start date. Testing dates may change due to inclement weather, however, the COTR shall first be notified and approve any changes necessary. Contractor shall anticipate all work to be done after normal working hours. Outages will be scheduled at night between the hours of 5:00 p.m. and midnight and between the hours of 7:00 am and 5:00 p.m. on weekends. However the Contractor should be prepared to work longer hours should problems develop to assure restoration of power. Daytime hours, during the week, may be approved under certain circumstances if there is no impact to building occupants. This would be a rare instance, thus Contractor should anticipate overtime hours for all contract requirements. Equipment Repairs: Minor repairs shall include but not be limited to such items as loose bolts, loose or broken lugs, wiring terminals, heaters, malfunctioning targets, dirty/high resistance connections, etc and shall be corrected on site during testing if possible. Repair or replacement of larger items such as breakers shall also be performed during this outage if possible. However if parts are not readily available, these items will be repaired or replaced under a separate smaller outage and will be scheduled after parts or components are available. Contractor shall set aside a line item not to exceed $50,000 for repair or replacement parts with this contract. All repairs shall be invoiced under this line item at the conclusion of the contract. This amount is to be used for bidding purposes. However a materials breakdown will be required with the final invoice and Contractor shall be paid actual costs with appropriate mark up s up to $50,000 for parts. Contractor is not to exceed this amount without prior written approval of the Contracting Officer. Minimum Equipment Test Requirements: 5 KV AIR CIRCUIT BREAKERS 1. The breakers will be removed from their compartments. The compartments shall be cleaned and inspected. Shutters shall be cleaned, inspected, and tested for proper operation. The racking mechanisms shall also be cleaned, lubricated and tested for proper operation. 2. All cable termination s, both primary and secondary, shall he checked for signs of overheating, proper tightness and support. 3. All exposed bus connections shall be checked for signs of overheating and for proper tightness. 4. The arc chutes will be removed, cleaned and inspected. 5. The entire breaker and the mechanism will be inspected. 6. The entire operating mechanism will be thoroughly cleaned, lubricated and exercised. 7. All of the interior components of the circuit breaker will be thoroughly cleaned. 8. The contacts and current carrying assemblies will be inspected for burning, pitting, arcing, worn fingers, garter springs etc. 9. The contacts will be cleaned and anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the breaker s main contacts. 10. The breaker contact resistance will be measured and recorded. 11. An insulation resistance test will be performed and results recorded. 12. The breaker will then be closed manually to ensure proper closing and trip operations. 13. Any and all interlocks will be checked and proper operation will be verified. 14. The breaker will be electrically operated when test stands are available, or the breaker will be operated from its cubicle, if the system allows. 15. All indicating devices such as lights, flags, switches etc. shall be tested for proper operation. Any that are not operating properly shall be repaired at that time if possible. 16. All heat strips throughout the enclosure shall be made operational, by repair or replacement, prior to completion of inspection. ENCLOSED AIR BREAK SWITCHES (MEDIUM VOLTAGE) 1. After shutdown, the entire switch mechanism will be cleaned and inspected. 2. The switch contacts will be checked for proper alignment. Anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the main contacts. 3. The switch s arcing contacts will be checked for the proper opening sequence relative to the main contacts. 4. The switch s operating mechanism will be inspected for wear and proper operation. The entire mechanism will be cleaned and lubricated. All interlocks will be tested and proper operation will be verified. 5. Fuses will be inspected; size and type will be recorded. 6. All phase isolation barriers will be cleaned, and the barriers will be checked for contamination and corona damage. 7. All insulators will be cleaned and visually inspected for cracks and chips. 8. All exposed bus and cable connections will be checked for proper tightness and for evidence of overheating, burning or tracking. 9. All lightning arrestors will be cleaned and inspected for broken or damaged porcelain and subjected to an insulation resistance test. Results shall be recorded. 10. All ground connections will be inspected and repaired if found to be inadequate. 11. Contact resistance and insulation resistance tests will be performed, where possible, and the results recorded. 12. All heat strips throughout the enclosure shall be made operational, by repair or replacement, prior to completion of inspection. OIL-FILLED TRANSFORMERS 1. title: J045--FY27 Boilers Maintenance & Testing
description: RFQ 36C24827Q0061 Amendment No. 1 This amendment is hereby issued to provide responses to questions and requests for information submitted by vendors, provide a revised PWS to address a correction on Boiler #2 description, as well as an updated Price/Cost Schedule reflecting the corrected description. Description of Boiler #2 contained on PWS and associated Line Items (LINs) of Price/Cost Schedule is hereby changed to read: Boiler Unit Number 2 (Local identifier): Fire tube steam boiler manufactured by York-Shipley; Serial number 96-19937-H-11618 The due date for Quote Submittal is changed from November 6, 2026, to November 10, 2026 at 10 AM AST. All other sections of the solicitation remain unchanged. RESPONSES TO QUESTIONS RECEIVED: Q1. Semiannual Safety-Device Testing: VHA Directive 1810, Appendix A, Section 2(a), establishes that safety devices requiring semiannual testing are ordinarily tested once annually by VA medical facility personnel and once annually by a qualified testing contractor, unless an alternative arrangement is approved. Does the Government require the contractor to perform both semiannual testing events under this solicitation? If so, has the alternative testing arrangement received the required approval? VACHS Boiler Plant personnel will perform the required semiannual safety-device testing. The Contractor shall perform the safety-device testing required under the PWS during its scheduled annual inspection and testing services. Q2. Monthly Safety Device Testing: PWS Section V(Q) includes safety-device tests for which the VHA Boiler and Associated Plant Safety Device Testing Manual establishes monthly testing frequencies, including primary and auxiliary low-water cutoffs, high- and low-water alarms, and the main flame-scanner flame-out test. Does the Government require the contractor to perform these tests monthly throughout the contract period, or will VACHS personnel continue performing the monthly tests while the contractor performs the scheduled maintenance and safety-device testing services? VACHS Boiler Plant personnel will perform the required monthly safety-device testing. Q3. Frequency of Nondestructive Testing, Component Replacement and Engineering Evaluations: PWS Sections V(I), V(L), V(U), V(V), and V(W) establish requirements involving component replacement, nondestructive testing (NDT), pressure-vessel inspections, and engineering evaluations, including ultrasonic thickness measurements, magnetic-particle examinations, and assessments of maximum allowable working pressure (MAWP) and remaining useful life. However, VHA Directive 1810, Appendix B, Table 2, establishes different inspection frequencies depending on the activity. For example, annual boiler inspections are required, whereas internal deaerator weld examinations using wet magnetic-particle testing are required at six-year intervals. Clarify the following: a. Nondestructive Testing: Are ultrasonic thickness measurements and magnetic-particle examinations required annually for each boiler and the deaerator, or are these examinations required only when indicated by inspection findings, equipment conditions, or established inspection intervals? The scope of this requirement applies to the Boilers only. b. Deaerator Weld Examination: Is the six-year internal deaerator weld examination required during the base contract period or any of the option years? If so, please identify the date of the most recent examination and the next scheduled examination. Not applicable. This service is cover under another service contract c. Engineering Evaluations: Are MAWP calculations, remaining-useful-life assessments, and deterioration-rate evaluations required annually for each boiler, deaerator, and condensate return tank, or only when inspection findings or equipment conditions warrant such evaluations? Not applicable. This service is not covered under this requirement. d. Component Replacement: Are component replacements identified in the PWS mandatory during each annual maintenance period, regardless of condition, or are replacements required only when inspection or testing establishes a deficiency, except where the PWS expressly requires replacement? Mandatory parts to be replaced annually during annual maintenance, regardless of its conditions: Sight glass with new seals, Compress air belt, oil filters, air filter, water gasket seal kits and fire side gaskets seal kit. e. Firetube Inspection Methods and Waterside Deterioration: PWS Section V(U) references fiberoptic inspection of boiler tubes, while Section V(V) establishes ultrasonic thickness measurement requirements. In a firetube boiler, fiberoptic examination from inside a tube primarily evaluates its fireside surface and does not directly establish the condition of the exterior waterside surface, where corrosion and pitting may occur. Please clarify whether the Government requires fiberoptic visual examination, ultrasonic thickness measurements, or additional examination methods capable of evaluating tube-wall deterioration affecting either surface. The Government requires the inspection methods specified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Fiberoptic inspection and ultrasonic thickness testing are complementary requirements, and both shall be performed. f. Boiler Tube Quantities and Technical Documentation: For each boiler, please identify the total number of firetubes, nominal tube diameter, original wall thickness or gauge, and applicable tube specifications. Please provide, if available, manufacturer drawings, tube-layout diagrams, pressure-vessel drawings, or other technical documentation identifying the shell, tube arrangements, tube sheets, and applicable pressure-retaining components, so that offerors can quantify the inspection scope. The Government has provided all available identifying information and that quotes/offers should be based on the PWS requirements and field verification. g. Extent of Tube Examination and Sampling Requirements: Does the Government require examination and wall-thickness measurements of every firetube in each boiler, or is an engineer-justified representative sampling program acceptable? If sampling is permitted, please identify any minimum sample quantity or percentage, prescribed examination locations, acceptance criteria, and requirements for expanding the examination when initial results reveal pitting, corrosion, thinning, or other deterioration. May the qualified inspecting engineer establish and justify the sampling methodology based on equipment condition, applicable standards, and inspection findings? The Government does not require examination or ultrasonic thickness measurements of every firetube. The Performance Work Statement requires inspection of a representative number of tubes and ultrasonic thickness testing of representative samples, with additional testing of areas exhibiting indications of corrosion, erosion, or other deterioration. The Contractor's Qualified Professional Inspector may establish and justify the sampling methodology using professional engineering judgment and applicable industry standards, provided the inspection is sufficient to assess equipment condition and support all required findings, calculations, and recommendations. h. Boiler shell examination and engineering certification: Please identify the required extent of ultrasonic thickness measurements and other nondestructive examinations of boiler shells, tube sheets, and other applicable pressure-retaining components. For the MAWP, deterioration-rate, and remaining-useful-life evaluations required by the PWS, does the Government require a formal report signed and sealed by a licensed Professional Engineer? Please identify any specified inspection coverage, minimum-thickness criteria, engineering standards, or historical thickness data to be used. Must the engineering determinations address the complete boiler pressure vessel, including firetubes and shell, or only components exam

description: This is a Special Notice of intent to award on a sole source basis. This is not a solicitation. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate a requirement for gym rental services for the VA Medical Center Northampton. The applicable NAICS code is 713940. The PSC/FSC is G003. The authority for this action is RFO FAR 12.102: Restricting competition and fulfills RFO FAR Part 5: Publicizing contract actions. This is a Special notice of intent to award on a sole source basis is to satisfy the requirements of RFO FAR 5.101. All interested parties should register via SAM.gov interested vendors list. It is the responsibility of the offeror to monitor and download amendments from SAM.gov Contract Opportunities, which may be issued to this notice. description: 3-Year Electrical Testing and Repair Contract Performance Work Statement (PWS) General Requirements: Contractor shall furnish all supplies, materials, equipment, personnel/labor and technical supervision required to perform inspections, repairs, testing, cleaning, calibrations and adjustments on the electrical power distribution system and associated equipment at the Hampton Veterans Affairs Medical Center within the allotted time frame of this contract. This is a 4160 volt primary system that includes various secondary voltages and both emergency and normal power sources. A comprehensive list of equipment is included in this contract as well as a dollar amount to be set aside for repairs. All inspections and testing procedures must meet the criteria of the original equipment manufacturer along with the latest editions of the following codes, standards and specifications listed: ANSI, IEEE, ICEA, NETA, NEMA, NFPA, JCAHO and VA regulations. The contractor shall be responsible for supplying all portable power required to power up any and all test equipment necessary throughout these tests. The use of normal or emergency building power will not be allowed. The contractor shall be responsible for securing all manufacturers information, curves, data, procedures and any other information necessary to conduct specific tests on equipment and systems. Prior to beginning field-testing, the testing organization shall submit test procedures and a detailed test schedule to the Electrical Supervisor for each item of equipment to be field-tested. No testing is to be performed until after the test procedures and schedules have been approved. The contractor shall be responsible for all coordination between Dominion Virginia Power (if applicable), station supervisory personnel and test personnel for scheduling shut-downs, system tests and tests on system components. The V.A Medical Center Electrical Staff will be responsible for conducting the actual scheduled outages and reenergizing of circuits and components on V.A. premises and V.A. owned equipment only. Lockout/Tagout of this equipment will be performed jointly between the V. A. Medical Center Electricians and the Contractor. The contractor will be responsible for removal and replacement of any and all breakers needing to be tested. All breakers being removed will be properly reinstalled. Any and all conductors removed from a breaker will be properly terminated back to that breaker and any and all lugs will be properly torqued to manufacturers specifications. Testing shall commence and be completed within nine (9) consecutive days, beginning on a Saturday and ending on the following Sunday. The specific dates shall be coordinated with the COTR. All outages shall be scheduled with the COTR two weeks in advance of testing start date. Testing dates may change due to inclement weather, however, the COTR shall first be notified and approve any changes necessary. Contractor shall anticipate all work to be done after normal working hours. Outages will be scheduled at night between the hours of 5:00 p.m. and midnight and between the hours of 7:00 am and 5:00 p.m. on weekends. However the Contractor should be prepared to work longer hours should problems develop to assure restoration of power. Daytime hours, during the week, may be approved under certain circumstances if there is no impact to building occupants. This would be a rare instance, thus Contractor should anticipate overtime hours for all contract requirements. Equipment Repairs: Minor repairs shall include but not be limited to such items as loose bolts, loose or broken lugs, wiring terminals, heaters, malfunctioning targets, dirty/high resistance connections, etc and shall be corrected on site during testing if possible. Repair or replacement of larger items such as breakers shall also be performed during this outage if possible. However if parts are not readily available, these items will be repaired or replaced under a separate smaller outage and will be scheduled after parts or components are available. Contractor shall set aside a line item not to exceed $50,000 for repair or replacement parts with this contract. All repairs shall be invoiced under this line item at the conclusion of the contract. This amount is to be used for bidding purposes. However a materials breakdown will be required with the final invoice and Contractor shall be paid actual costs with appropriate mark up s up to $50,000 for parts. Contractor is not to exceed this amount without prior written approval of the Contracting Officer. Minimum Equipment Test Requirements: 5 KV AIR CIRCUIT BREAKERS 1. The breakers will be removed from their compartments. The compartments shall be cleaned and inspected. Shutters shall be cleaned, inspected, and tested for proper operation. The racking mechanisms shall also be cleaned, lubricated and tested for proper operation. 2. All cable termination s, both primary and secondary, shall he checked for signs of overheating, proper tightness and support. 3. All exposed bus connections shall be checked for signs of overheating and for proper tightness. 4. The arc chutes will be removed, cleaned and inspected. 5. The entire breaker and the mechanism will be inspected. 6. The entire operating mechanism will be thoroughly cleaned, lubricated and exercised. 7. All of the interior components of the circuit breaker will be thoroughly cleaned. 8. The contacts and current carrying assemblies will be inspected for burning, pitting, arcing, worn fingers, garter springs etc. 9. The contacts will be cleaned and anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the breaker s main contacts. 10. The breaker contact resistance will be measured and recorded. 11. An insulation resistance test will be performed and results recorded. 12. The breaker will then be closed manually to ensure proper closing and trip operations. 13. Any and all interlocks will be checked and proper operation will be verified. 14. The breaker will be electrically operated when test stands are available, or the breaker will be operated from its cubicle, if the system allows. 15. All indicating devices such as lights, flags, switches etc. shall be tested for proper operation. Any that are not operating properly shall be repaired at that time if possible. 16. All heat strips throughout the enclosure shall be made operational, by repair or replacement, prior to completion of inspection. ENCLOSED AIR BREAK SWITCHES (MEDIUM VOLTAGE) 1. After shutdown, the entire switch mechanism will be cleaned and inspected. 2. The switch contacts will be checked for proper alignment. Anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the main contacts. 3. The switch s arcing contacts will be checked for the proper opening sequence relative to the main contacts. 4. The switch s operating mechanism will be inspected for wear and proper operation. The entire mechanism will be cleaned and lubricated. All interlocks will be tested and proper operation will be verified. 5. Fuses will be inspected; size and type will be recorded. 6. All phase isolation barriers will be cleaned, and the barriers will be checked for contamination and corona damage. 7. All insulators will be cleaned and visually inspected for cracks and chips. 8. All exposed bus and cable connections will be checked for proper tightness and for evidence of overheating, burning or tracking. 9. All lightning arrestors will be cleaned and inspected for broken or damaged porcelain and subjected to an insulation resistance test. Results shall be recorded. 10. All ground connections will be inspected and repaired if found to be inadequate. 11. Contact resistance and insulation resistance tests will be performed, where possible, and the results recorded. 12. All heat strips throughout the enclosure shall be made operational, by repair or replacement, prior to completion of inspection. OIL-FILLED TRANSFORMERS 1. title: Stage 2 - Sidney Operations Centre Marine Fuel & Docks Replacement, Gulf Islands National Park Reserve
description: Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing docks and marine fueling system at the Sidney Operations Centre (SOC), located at 2220 Harbour Road in Sidney, British Columbia, which serves as the primary Parks Canada Agency office and marine operations base for the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. The work includes the removal, disposal, and replacement of the existing docks, pilings, and associated servicing systems. The Contractor will supply and install new aluminum-frame docks, pilings, water and electrical services, dock lighting, and a new fueling system consisting of a 5,000-litre fuel tank, fuel lines, and dispenser. All in-water works, including the removal of the existing docks and pilings and the installation of the new docks, must be completed within the lower-risk fisheries window between December 1, 2026, and February 15, 2027. Work occurring above the high-water line may be completed outside of this period. The Contractor will be required to implement the mitigation measures identified in Parks Canada Agency’s Basic Impact Assessment to minimize environmental risks and impacts associated with the project. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

title: Stage 2 - Lake Annette Retaining Wall Replacement, Jasper National Park
description: REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing retaining wall and reconstruct the adjacent pathway along the Lake Annette Loop Trail in Jasper National Park, Alberta. The project involves the replacement of approximately 110 m of deteriorated retaining wall and the reconstruction of the adjacent 2.0 m wide asphalt pathway located between Lake Annette and Ochre Lake within a high-use day-use area. Construction is anticipated to take place during Fall 2026 to reduce impacts on peak visitor use and take advantage of lower seasonal water levels. The existing natural stone retaining wall has experienced progressive deterioration, resulting in wall instability, pavement cracking, material loss, localized shoreline erosion, and reduced visitor safety. The objective of the project is to restore shoreline stability, improve visitor safety, and provide a durable, low-maintenance infrastructure solution that is compatible with the surrounding natural environment. The Contractor will be responsible for all labour, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to complete the work, including demolition and disposal of the existing retaining wall and pathway, excavation and foundation preparation, installation of a new segmented retaining wall with geogrid reinforcement, reconstruction of the asphalt pathway, drainage improvements, and site clean-up. All work shall be carried out in accordance with the issued engineering drawings, technical specifications, environmental requirements, and contract documents. Revegetation and landscape restoration are not included in this contract and will be solicited separately. Given the environmentally sensitive nature of the site, the Contractor must minimize impacts to adjacent wetlands, shoreline habitat, and visitor-use facilities. VETERINARY WASTE AND ANIMAL CARCASSES: Animal parts, carcasses, waste tissue and other veterinary waste packed in tied and leak-proof RED BAGS . Pathologic specimens, including human or animal tissues, blood elements, excreta and secretions which contain etiologic agents and attendant disposable fomites. Surgical specimens, including human or animal parts and tissues removed surgically or at autopsy which contains etiologic agents and attendant disposable fomites. Equipment, instruments, utensils and other disposable materials which are likely to transmit etiologic agents from the room of humans, or the enclosures of animals which have been isolated because of suspected or diagnosed communicable disease. Human dialysis waste materials including arterial lines and dialysate membranes. Carcasses of animals infected with etiologic agents which may present a substance hazard to public health if improperly managed. Any other material which, in the determination of the facility infection control staff, presents a significant danger of infection because it is contaminated with or may reasonably be expected to be contaminated with etiologic agents. title: Ireland – Training services – Request for Tenders dated October 22nd 2026 for the provision of ICT Training via an Online Training Platform
description: The Revenue Commissioners (Revenue) is seeking a provider of an e-learning platform to support the continuing professional development of staff in its ICT function. Revenue requires a platform for 200 users that provides access to relevant, high-quality learning content on current technologies and industry practices. The platform should have a clear, intuitive catalogue that enables users to easily search for and access relevant learning materials. The provider must ensure that content is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect developments in technology and industry practices. The successful provider will also be expected to provide a responsive customer success team that works collaboratively with Revenue to support the effective use of the platform and adapt to Revenue’s evolving learning needs throughout the contract term.

title: NWI Offsite Pathology Services
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Nebraska-Western Iowa Health Care System , has a requirement for medical laboratory, pathology and testing analysis services. The Contractor shall be responsible for performing pre-analytic processing as defined in its laboratory manual, analysis, and reporting of analytical results and interpretation for clinical and anatomical pathology specimens as requested by participating facilities (listed below) during the contract period. The contractor shall provide Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services, on a scheduled basis, in accordance with the specifications, terms and conditions herein. VA will be responsible for specimen collection, preparation, grossing (with the exception of, cytology specimens); global surgical pathology cases would require grossing by the contractor. The VA will accession histology and cytology cases, VistA accessioning, preservation and storage of final slides and blocks. All slides and blocks must be returned to the VA for permanent storage.

Project Overview This project addresses replacement of dental vacuum pumps, fluid separators, and associated components at Ft McPherson Medical/Dental Clinic, Building 125. Scope includes replacement of defective pumps, defective fluid separation, defective amalgam separation, and defective control panels. Ensure all installations are compatible with existing pipes and equipment to remain. All work shall comply with VA Design Manuals. Work shall result in a complete and working dental vacuum system. No equipment is to be ordered, and no work shall begin until field-verified dimensions are submitted and approved by VA Engineering Department. The Contractor is responsible for coordinating measurement activities with facility engineering and ensuring all site-specific constraints are factored into submittals and planning. 3. Equipment History and Impacts The existing AirTech Dental Vacuum System has exhibited multiple pump and oral fluid storage failures over the last two years. The system exhibits signs of antiquation and inferior design. The components of the existing system differ from current market standards and may result in undesired storage condition of biohazardous fluid. Undesired fluid storage presents environmental concern and costly breakdown of system components. Strict adherence to Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO) requirements for all energy sources throughout the course of work, with full documentation submitted for VA records. Comply with all VA and OSHA site safety protocols (including PPE, daily housekeeping, and mandatory orientation). Perform full Risk Assessment in coordination with VA Infection Control and Safety staff. The forms and requirements shall be approved before any work can take place. This shall implement and maintain all required barriers, negative air systems, and infection prevention measures specified in the PCRA. Secure written VA approval for all shutdowns or disruptions to critical clinic operations. 6. description: **NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE** This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) RFO 5.101(a) Presolicitation notice requirements and (FAR) RFO 12.102 Restricting Competition. This Notice of Intent is for a proposed award of an open market sole source award to Vicinity Energy Baltimore Corporation for an annual steam system preventative maintenance contract at the VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS) Baltimore VAMC located at 10 North Greene St. Baltimore, MD 21201. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this service is 561210 (Facilities Support Services). Product Service Code (PSC) is J044 (Maintenance, Repair and Rebuilding of Equipment Furnace, Steam Plant, and Drying Equipment; Nuclear Reactors). Small business size standard is $47.0 Million. While this synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency, by emailing such statement and supporting documentation by NLT 11:00 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST), 11/10/2026 to Contract Specialist Patricia Thai via email at Patricia.Thai@va.gov. Please reference the announcement number (36C24527Q0048) in the subject line of the e-mail. Such documentation will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct the procurement on a competitive basis. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government under authorities cited above. Statement of Work (SOW) Baltimore VAMC Steam Maintenance Service Contract Introduction: This contract covers all maintenance, repairs, preventive maintenance (PM), and emergency call-back services for the steam system at the Baltimore VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 10 North Greene Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. The Contractor shall perform all services necessary to ensure reliable operation of steam system components and maintain them in accordance with industry standards and manufacturer recommendations. Baltimore VAMC s in-building steam equipment is directly connected to Vicinity Energy s district steam distribution system, which Vicinity owns and operates throughout downtown Baltimore. Because of this interconnected configuration, any work performed on the customer side components can affect not only the Baltimore VAMC but also Vicinity s broader distribution network. No other company owns or operates comparable district steam infrastructure in Baltimore. Therefore, maintenance activities require close coordination with Vicinity s system operations, pressure management, isolation sequencing, and startup/shutdown procedures. Vicinity s technical personnel also maintain proprietary operational data and engineering knowledge that is not readily accessible to third party contractors. A comprehensive preventive maintenance (PM) program would deliver several key benefits: Reliability Reduces outages, operational disruptions, and unexpected system failures Cost Savings Identifies issues early, preventing more costly future repairs Equipment Performance Supports safer, more efficient operation of critical steam dependent systems System Longevity Extends the lifespan and performance of essential steam infrastructure Scope of Services: The Contractor shall provide a two-person crew for eight (8) hours every two weeks (totaling 416 labor hours per year) to maintain steam system components, including: Performing steam trap surveys Cleaning pressure-reducing valves Inspecting heat exchangers and steam converters Ensuring proper operation of condensate tanks, pumps, and piping Identifying and addressing steam piping or valve leaks Verifying proper operation of all meters Ensuring proper water chemistry Assisting with regulatory inspections Parts and Materials: The Contractor shall supply all parts, materials, equipment, and tools necessary to complete the work described. All replacement parts shall meet the original manufacturer s specifications or be approved equivalents. Emergency Service: The Contractor shall provide prompt emergency call-back service within five (5) hours of notification by the Contracting Officer (CO), Contracting Officer s Representative (COR), or their designees. A qualified service technician must be on site within five (5) hours when emergency repairs are required due to system shutdowns or critical issues arising between scheduled service visits. Service Reporting: Upon completion of each PM service, the Contractor shall submit a written report to the COR detailing the services performed, corrective actions taken, parts used, and recommendations for extending the useful life of steam system components. General Information, Requirements and Expectations: The Contractor shall check in with the Plumbing Shop or Utility Systems Repairer Operator (USRO) Supervisors upon arrival at the facility. An emergency telephone number must be provided for urgent repair needs. Contractor personnel are required to wear uniforms that display the company name in a clear and permanent manner for easy identification. Tour of Duty: All routine work will be performed during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM, except in cases of emergency call-back. Routine maintenance should not be scheduled on observed Federal Holidays. Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is one (1) year from the contract award date, with potential option-year periods to be exercised at the Government s discretion. Place of Performance: All work shall be performed at Baltimore VA Medical Center (VAMC) 10 North Greene Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. Security, Safety, and Access Requirements: Contractor personnel shall follow all VA security, safety, and infection control requirements. Contractor vehicles, tools, and equipment may be subject to inspection. The Contractor shall ensure adherence to all facility safety policies and immediately report unsafe conditions to the COR.

title: AJ11--Supine to Seated or Standing Lumbar Spine MRI Scan Services
description: DESCRIPTION This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and planning purposes. This notice is intended to identify potential sources that possess the capabilities, experience, and resources necessary to provide the services described herein. This is not a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Regional Procurement Office (RPO) East, is conducting market research to determine the availability of qualified sources capable of providing specialized lumbar spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan services in support of a VA research study. The purpose of this notice is to determine the availability of qualified small and large business concerns and to assist the Government in acquisition planning, including potential socioeconomic set-aside considerations. Interested firms are encouraged to identify their business size and socioeconomic status. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 621512, Diagnostic Imaging Centers. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used for market research purposes only. Responses are not considered offers and will not be evaluated for award. Interested parties must respond separately to any future solicitation announcement. There is no solicitation at this time. The Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred in responding to this notice. Interested parties shall not submit pricing information. Questions regarding this notice shall be submitted via email to millicent.covert@va.gov. SCOPE Specific Tasks and Deliverables This study requires MRI scans while the subject is seated or standing to allow body weight loading of the lumbar spine. The scanning facility shall possess MRI equipment capable of imaging subjects in both supine and weight-bearing (standing or seated) positions. The Government prefers a system that allows imaging in both positions without requiring the subject to exit and re-enter the scanner. The anticipated study population is approximately thirty-nine (39) participants over a four-year period beginning on or about January 1, 2027. The Contractor shall provide the following: Pre-Whole Body Vibration (WBV) MRI Series One (1) lumbar spine supine MRI scan. One (1) lumbar spine weight-bearing MRI scan. Total pre-WBV MRI time shall not exceed sixty (60) minutes. Post-Whole Body Vibration (WBV) MRI Series One (1) lumbar spine supine MRI scan. One (1) lumbar spine weight-bearing MRI scan. Total post-WBV MRI time shall not exceed sixty (60) minutes. Contractor Requirements The Contractor shall: Be located within one hundred (100) miles of the Clement J. Zablocki VA Medical Center, Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Provide certified MRI technologists to perform all scans. Provide access to a private room for subject exposure to thirty (30) minutes of whole-body vibration. The VA research team will furnish the vibration table and chair. Perform all MRI scans described above. The VA study team will coordinate with the Contractor regarding the MRI sequences necessary to achieve study objectives within the required timeframe. Provide a standard clinical interpretation of each pre-WBV MRI scan by a licensed radiologist affiliated with the imaging facility. Reports shall include findings by spinal level and overall regional assessment. De-identified PDF reports shall be provided within two (2) weeks of the scan date. Maintain participant confidentiality through the use of study-specific identifiers supplied by the VA study team. Provide secure electronic access to all imaging studies. Data transfer shall occur through VA-approved secure file-sharing methods. Provide suitable laboratory space for VA personnel to measure urine specific gravity samples using VA-furnished equipment. VA personnel will be responsible for sample handling and disposal. RESPONSE REQUIREMENTS Interested parties shall submit the following information: 1. Company Information Provide: Company name Physical and mailing address Website address Point of Contact (POC) Telephone number Email address Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code 2. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status Identify your firm's business size under NAICS Code 621512 and indicate all applicable socioeconomic classifications, including: Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) 8(a) Business Development Program Participant HUBZone Small Business Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Large Business Provide: Business structure (e.g., Corporation, LLC, Partnership, Sole Proprietorship) Active SAM registration status SAM registration information is available at https://sam.gov/. If claiming a socioeconomic designation, identify the applicable certification program and certification status. NOTE: Any future contract award may only be made to an entity with an active registration in SAM.gov. Firms seeking consideration under a socioeconomic set-aside program must satisfy all applicable eligibility and certification requirements at the time of offer submission and contract award. 3. title: DNWP0027- Lot 1B / WAGR B55 Demolition - Sellafield - A2R JV
description: The B55 and B55.2 demolition project at Sellafield involves the controlled demolition and dismantling of the B55 Office Complex and B55.2 Turbine Hall, located within the WAGR complex, down to existing ground-floor slab level. The scope includes soft stripping, asbestos remediation, high-reach mechanical demolition of the structural frame, cladding and reinforced-concrete floors, together with segregation and processing of demolition arisings, backfilling of voids and final site clearance. A key constraint is Substation 65, which is located within the B55/B55.2 structure and must remain operational and be protected from demolition impacts, dust and water ingress throughout the works. Retained basements and associated structures also require protection, while uncertainties associated with ageing structures, buried services, below-ground voids and incomplete historical information must be managed through robust surveys, demolition engineering and risk-informed planning. Overall, the project is intended to provide a safe, demolition-led solution that reduces workforce exposure, removes redundant infrastructure and supports accelerated hazard reduction across the wider WAGR decommissioning programme. Additional information: https://www.linkedin.com/company/a2r-altrad-atkinsrealis-remediation https://www.gov.uk/government/news/sellafield-ltd-awards-high-hazard-risk-reduction-framework-contract

title: Candidate Assessment Services
description: Ingeus is seeking a specialist assessment platform provider to support clinical and non-clinical volume and specialist recruitment for the Health Assessment Advisory Service (HAAS). The requirement includes hosting bespoke assessment tools that have already been created as one element of a wider recruitment process. It may also include supplier-recommended assessment types, such as video situational judgement tests or work sample assessments. The successful supplier will be responsible for hosting the assessments; scoring and evaluating responses; managing candidate access; and providing assessment reports and outcomes to authorised Ingeus recruitment stakeholders for internal use and to support constructive feedback for applicant review. The supplier must hold the appropriate intellectual property rights, licences and assessment methodologies required to deliver and evaluate the assessments. Ingeus will not independently administer, score or evaluate proprietary assessments. Due to time constraints, the solution should already be compatible with Ingeus's existing SmartRecruiters platform and provide an integrated, seamless internal and external user experience. Suppliers should provide information covering: · Experience delivering recruitment assessment solutions for high-volume recruitment campaigns, including relevant client examples. · How the proposed solution assesses behavioral characteristics such as resilience, conscientiousness and emotional regulation. · Existing capability to integrate with SmartRecruiters and any implementation considerations. · Accessibility features and reasonable adjustment provisions available to users. · Compliance with UK GDPR and relevant security accreditations, for example ISO 27001 and/or Cyber Essentials Plus. · Confirmation that the supplier is a UK-registered organisation and that candidate data is hosted and processed within the UK. · Pricing for development, build, implementation, licenses and users. · Development and/or build and implementation timescales. · Technical environment dependencies. · User restriction parameters or policies. Shortlisted suppliers may be required to provide further information relating to architecture, information security, compliance, integration and support as part of the evaluation. Additional information: Responses and any enquiries should be submitted by email by/before the closing date stated above, with "Candidate Assessment Services" in the subject field

title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Purchase Order: HeinOnline U.S. Core+ for Government Subscription
description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) intends to award a firm-fixed-price Purchase Order, on a sole source basis, to William S. Hein & Co., Inc., 2350 North Forest Road, Getzville, NY 14068. The Purchase Order is for an enterprise subscription to the HeinOnline U.S. Core+ for Government electronic database. The subscription will have a 12-month base period, November 16, 2026 through November 15, 2027, and three 12-month option periods. The CFPB will use simplified acquisition procedures under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13. The authority for this sole source action is RFO FAR 13.101(b). The anticipated award date is by November 16, 2026. William S. Hein & Co., Inc. is the only publisher of HeinOnline and holds the exclusive rights to its content and platform. The CFPB needs complete, true-to-print, image-based historical coverage of the U.S. Statutes at Large, U.S. Code, Federal Register, Code of Federal Regulations, and Congressional Record, together with the law journal, treatise, and case law content in the U.S. Core+ for Government collection. This action is at or below the simplified acquisition threshold. This notice is the solicitation for this requirement. It is posted to SAM.gov and permits the public to respond electronically, under RFO FAR 5.101(b)(1)(i). The CFPB intends to award to William S. Hein & Co., Inc. Any firm that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement or quote to patrick.sisk@cfpb.gov by Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time. A response must show clearly that the firm can provide this requirement, including written authorization from William S. Hein & Co., Inc. to resell HeinOnline, if applicable. The CFPB will consider all responses received by the response date. A decision not to compete this requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. No phone calls, please.
